name: 3-oa
title: OA — Operational analysis
subtitle: How the tasked area is watched and reported today, with no system named: the entities, what each does, what they exchange, and the operational modes and states.

steps.label: SHOW ONLY THE OA LAYER
steps.text: In the Explorer, ⊞ on OA scopes every diagram to the operational-analysis package. The chip above the canvas says what is shown.

steps.label: GENERAL VIEW
steps.text: All of OA as boxes, read left to right: the people, drones and ground equipment of today's operation, and the activities allocated to each. No system is named.

steps.label: READ ONE ELEMENT
steps.text: Select a box: Properties shows what it is. memberA stands for one of the twelve drones, not an extra one. The purple lines on its left: the 14 activities it performs.

steps.label: TREE VIEW
steps.text: What OA contains, one branch at a time. +N on a box opens what it owns: here the action definition HandOverSector and its two ports, one out and one in.

steps.label: INTERCONNECTION VIEW
steps.text: The twelve kinds of entity and their fourteen usages: people, drones, ground station, radios, recharge and recovery points, cameras. No connections at OA.

steps.label: ACTION VIEW
steps.text: The 38 activities, each allocated to the entity that performs it. No successions: at OA they are a set, not a sequence. The lines are the 33 flows between them, each labelled with what it carries.

steps.label: STATE VIEW
steps.text: Four state machines: one drone's sortie and its operating condition, the fleet's mission and its mesh. Lines are transitions; most are labelled trigger / effect.

steps.label: READ ONE STATE MACHINE
steps.text: A drone that loses satellite positioning goes from Nominal to NavigationDegraded and navigates by camera; when positioning is back it resumes satellite navigation.

steps.label: CASE VIEW
steps.text: The mission, WatchTheTaskedArea, and ten capabilities as use cases. Each names its subject, holder: a drone, the duty controller or the analyst.

steps.label: REQUIREMENT VIEW
steps.text: OA's hazards, each satisfied by an activity. Before recording we deleted one, ReportLostInLinkGapHazard, and its «satisfy» went with it. Now we add it back.

steps.label: SELECT WHERE IT GOES
steps.text: A new element goes under the selection, so first select the Hazards package, inside OA, in the Explorer.

steps.label: PLACE A REQUIREMENT
steps.text: Pick Requirement in the palette, then click empty canvas. The new requirement is created in Hazards and selected.

steps.label: GIVE IT ITS TEXT
steps.text: The statement goes in Requirement text, word for word as in the model: a report is sent into a link gap and nobody knows it never arrived.

do.type: A detection report is sent into a link gap and nobody knows it never arrived.

steps.label: TAG IT AND NAME ITS SUBJECT
steps.text: Tags takes the #Hazard keyword, which resolves to Kinds::Hazard. Subject takes name : Type: the hazard is about holder, the operations-centre analyst.

steps.label: ITS «SATISFY» GOES IN GENERAL
steps.text: acknowledgeReports, which satisfied it, left the Requirement view with it; General shows both. Select it and press Selection, then pick Satisfy and click it: the satisfier first.

steps.label: THEN CLICK THE REQUIREMENT
steps.text: The strip above the canvas now asks for the target. Fit, zoom to the new hazard and click it: the «satisfy» is drawn, and filed in OA, where it was.

steps.label: THE RESULT
steps.text: The Requirement view is as it was: four hazards, each satisfied by an activity, and the hazard has its tag and subject back. Not re-entered: SA's «satisfy» of it, which lives in SA. Edits stay in this browser until saved or exported.

outro.title: SA — System analysis
outro.text: The system as one black box: the functions it performs, the actors it serves, the modes it can be in and the requirements it meets. The live model: cosmindxu.github.io/mbse-workflow
